diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber-facing router TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold. The EPON link, OLT, VLAN, RADIUS state, and customer session are otherwise healthy, so the fault is isolated to router reachability or router management telemetry.
evidence: The router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, which is in the danger range above 4 hours.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has healthy CPU, memory, temperature, and all eight PONs marked healthy, ruling out an OLT-wide failure.
The target ONU is online and responding with normal RX power of -20.61 dBm and TX power of 2.40 dBm.
The seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable, distance remains constant at 152, and TX bias remains within the healthy range, ruling out fibre, distance, and laser degradation.
All visible peers on EPON0/2 are online, so there is no shared PON or splitter fault.
The customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1062, RADIUS exists and matches CRM, and the customer has an active session with normal re-authentication frequency.
The stale router heartbeat is therefore the only current abnormality and is best classified as router_unreachable.

remediation.action: Check the router's power, management interface, upstream connectivity, and monitoring path. Attempt out-of-band access or an ICMP/SNMP probe, inspect router and uplink logs, and restore/restart the router or its management service if required. Verify heartbeat recovery and customer traffic afterward; do not dispatch fibre or PON work based on these readings.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
